scope: Selected public primary sources; not exhaustive, and no hardware replication.

sources.title: Sharing AI progress in mathematics
sources.publisher: OpenAI
sources.status: Mixed verification; not independently checked here
sources.readScope: Official announcement and openai/math README; repository HEAD 1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a recorded; no individual proof or Lean build audited.
sources.claim: OpenAI released mathematical manuscripts and supporting formalizations from an internal model. The repository explicitly distinguishes results with and without formal proofs.
sources.limit: An announcement, a manuscript, and a kernel-checked theorem are different evidence levels. Mathematical results do not validate a physical device or establish that a simulated mechanism exists.
sources.application: Keep each hypothesis linked to its exact assumptions, source version, executable checks, and unresolved claims.

sources.title: Research acceleration: The view inside OpenAI
sources.publisher: OpenAI
sources.readScope: Main report and methodology appendix; underlying private logs unavailable.
sources.claim: The report tracks increasing agent use, code production, and experimental activity inside OpenAI, alongside continued human steering.
sources.limit: Compute availability also increased. Correlated productivity metrics do not isolate a causal AI effect or measure the correctness of new physical theories.
sources.application: Track valid experiments, failed checks, and reproducible results instead of counting only generated hypotheses or code.

sources.title: Discovering state-of-the-art quantum circuits with large language models
sources.publisher: Gu, Kemeny, Yelin and Lukin; Anthropic / Harvard / QuEra
sources.status: Preprint; author results, not replicated here
sources.readScope: Abstract, introduction, evaluator formulation, and design-principles section of v1; appendices not fully audited.
sources.claim: Candidate circuits are checked by an independent program and ranked by resource cost. The paper reports both resource counts improving for seven tasks and a trade-off improvement for the eighth.
sources.limit: The evaluator exploits a restricted circuit class; this is not a universal efficient quantum simulator. Circuit resource reductions are not observed quantum hardware performance or evidence of antigravity.
sources.application: Separate candidate generation from deterministic constraint checking; publish both objective and correctness failures.

sources.title: Claude Science, an AI workbench for scientists
sources.publisher: Anthropic
sources.readScope: Official product announcement; product not installed or benchmarked.
sources.claim: The workbench combines scientific tools, compute orchestration, and artifacts with histories intended to support audit and reproduction.
sources.limit: Vendor examples do not establish accuracy across disciplines; access to many tools does not resolve model error or supply missing experimental observations.
sources.application: Export a run record containing inputs, equations, software version, results, and limitations alongside every visualization.

sources.title: Previewing the Model Hardware Standard
sources.publisher: Anthropic
sources.status: Partner preview; not a verified public SDK integration
sources.readScope: Overview, driver/command description, and reported limitations; no SDK executed.
sources.claim: MHS proposes a shared device interface with discoverable capabilities, metadata, and commands for scientific and manufacturing equipment.
sources.limit: The announcement describes an early partner preview ahead of open sourcing. Reported model errors show that an interface does not confer physical understanding or safe autonomous operation.
sources.application: Describe virtual instruments through explicit units, operating bounds, readouts, and a simulation-only mode; do not imply connection to real hardware.

sources.title: Learning Physical Operators using Neural Operators
sources.publisher: Gopakumar et al.; PMLR / AISTATS 2026
sources.readScope: Proceedings metadata plus PDF abstract, weaknesses, and Appendix D; experiments not reproduced.
sources.claim: The method separates physical operators and uses a neural ODE formulation for continuous-time prediction, evaluated on fluid equations.
sources.limit: The paper uses an additive spatial decomposition, not sequential fractional time steps. Its tested boundary conditions are periodic; choosing a useful decomposition still requires physical expertise.
sources.application: Keep source, propagation, boundary, and loss modules explicit; test each component and changes of scale separately.

sources.title: Physics-informed Neural Operator Learning for Nonlinear Grad-Shafranov Equation
sources.publisher: Ding et al.; PMLR / ICML 2026
sources.readScope: Proceedings metadata plus PDF abstract, conclusion, operational-comparison section, and Appendix E; author code not executed.
sources.claim: The authors combine data anchors with equation residuals and study prediction under distribution shifts in fixed-boundary plasma equilibrium.
sources.limit: Reported error compares with an operational equilibrium solver; the study assumes static, fixed-boundary equilibria. Free-boundary coil coupling and closed-loop transient control remain outside this model.
sources.application: Validate boundary conditions and known reference solutions, then test withheld parameter regimes before trusting optimized designs.

sources.title: j-Wave: Differentiable acoustic simulations in JAX
sources.publisher: UCL Biomedical Ultrasound Group / j-Wave contributors
sources.readScope: README, pyproject (0.2.1, LGPL-3.0-only), and selected time_harmonic.py functions. HEAD d1918f4e6adbf3822108e0af8034063efed1d581; file header permits later LGPL versions.
sources.claim: A modular acoustic simulation framework uses JAX differentiation and compilation with CPU/GPU/TPU execution paths.
sources.limit: The inspected angular-spectrum function explicitly omits absorption. The Helmholtz wrapper returns a solution without forwarding the solver status; a later integration should check its residual independently.
sources.application: A future high-fidelity acoustic backend can use parameter gradients; compare them with finite differences and verify convergence before using them for design.

sources.title: Meep electromagnetic simulation and adjoint design
sources.publisher: Meep / NanoComp contributors
sources.readScope: Adjoint overview, derivative convergence example, multilayer example, and repository license listing (GPL-2.0). Observed repository HEAD: e1ff04e62514c4860f917c52ca33977180dfdaee.
sources.claim: Meep models electromagnetic fields with FDTD and provides gradients for supported objectives; its tutorial explicitly compares adjoint and finite-difference derivatives.
sources.limit: Grid resolution, boundary treatment, material models, and objective definition affect the answer. A local field-intensity objective is not automatically transmitted power.
sources.application: Compare exact reduced models with a converged field solver and test several starting designs before making an optimization claim.

sources.title: MuJoCo: Multi-Joint dynamics with Contact
sources.publisher: Google DeepMind / MuJoCo contributors
sources.readScope: README capability and licensing sections; source Apache-2.0, documentation/media CC BY 4.0. Observed repository HEAD: 9f035384db1a0f023c68fb8388e736f8ff811f73.
sources.claim: MuJoCo supplies a physics engine for articulated bodies and contact, with applications including robotics and model-based control.
sources.limit: Rigid-body/contact simulations do not themselves solve acoustic scattering or Maxwell fields. Attractive animation is not a measurement of an unmodeled force.
sources.application: Use only for later mechanical mounts or moving components, coupled to an independently validated force model.

sources.title: Cirq quantum circuit framework
sources.publisher: Quantum AI / Cirq contributors
sources.readScope: README capabilities and Apache-2.0 license listing. Observed repository HEAD: 501345094cb1c2a7eff4f7e83e0a3e303702a6bc.
sources.claim: Cirq supports circuit construction, transformations, noise models, and simulation, with interfaces to quantum devices.
sources.limit: Classical simulation cost can grow rapidly with qubit count. A simulated quantum circuit is a mathematical information-processing model, not evidence of macroscopic levitation.
sources.application: Keep any future quantum demo small and check unitarity, normalization, and measurement statistics against analytic cases.

sources.title: Building on our commitment to American scientific discovery
sources.publisher: Anthropic
sources.readScope: Official company announcement; funding disbursement and project outcomes not independently audited.
sources.claim: Anthropic describes a three-year commitment to provide AI access and support to projects in the US Genesis Mission.
sources.limit: A funding commitment or agency affiliation establishes program participation, not validation of a particular device, force, or energy claim.
sources.application: Separate program provenance and planned research from published methods and replicated physical observations.

sources.title: Opticks, Book III: observations and Query 31
sources.publisher: Isaac Newton; scholarly transcription by the Newton Project
sources.readScope: Opening diffraction observations and Query 31 closing analysis/synthesis discussion, printed pp. 380–382; normalized transcription, not every manuscript image.
sources.claim: Newton separates observations, inference about causes, and further consequences to be examined experimentally.
sources.limit: The Queries contain exploratory suggestions. They do not establish a modern quantum or frequency-healing mechanism.
sources.application: Keep measured input, fitted model, forward prediction, and independent test as separate stages.

sources.title: Of Natures obvious laws & processes in vegetation
sources.publisher: Isaac Newton; Indiana University Chymistry of Isaac Newton
sources.date: Manuscript date not assigned here; digital edition 2006
sources.readScope: Catalogue metadata, opening propositions and similarities/dissimilarities, plus concluding distinction between mechanical rearrangement and vegetation.
sources.claim: Newton explored analogies between mineral and living processes, including a proposed latent spirit.
sources.limit: Historical vocabulary is not an operational definition of a field, energy source, or biological mechanism.
sources.application: Turn an analogy into a declared variable map, then test where that map fails.

sources.title: Hermes / Tabula Smaragdina, Keynes MS. 28
sources.publisher: Newton manuscript; Indiana University scholarly edition
sources.date: Manuscript date not assigned here; digital edition June 2010
sources.readScope: Metadata and English Emerald Tablet text on folios 2r–2v; the Latin commentary was not translated in full.
sources.claim: The manuscript preserves a Hermetic text about correspondences, transformation and unity.
sources.limit: Copying or translating a text is not proof of its physical claims, nor evidence of a modern levitation device.
sources.application: Use correspondence as a question about mathematical similarity, with an explicit failure case.

sources.title: US645576A — System of transmission of electrical energy
sources.publisher: Nikola Tesla; US patent publication mirrored by Google Patents
sources.readScope: Publication metadata; source, transmitting/receiving transformers, atmospheric-conduction assumption, synchronism and loss passages; OCR text.
sources.claim: The proposal includes an electrical source, a propagation medium, tuned receiving circuits and a load.
sources.limit: This patent does not provide independently verified global power-transfer efficiency. A lumped coupled-resonator model is not a reconstruction of its atmospheric channel.
sources.application: Model source-to-load efficiency and detuning while retaining coupling and losses.

sources.title: US685957A — Apparatus for the utilization of radiant energy
sources.publisher: Nikola Tesla; US patent publication mirrored by Google Patents
sources.readScope: Publication metadata; external radiation, accumulation, discharge/load passages and claims 2–7 in OCR text.
sources.claim: A collector and capacitor receive energy from an external source, then discharge through a receiving circuit.
sources.limit: External radiation and any auxiliary circuit supply belong in the energy budget. Historical microscopic explanations are not adopted as modern physics.
sources.application: Compare accumulated input, stored energy, delivered work and losses over the same interval.

sources.title: Colorado Springs Notes, June 21–22, 1899, page 43
sources.publisher: Tesla notebook; Tesla Universe transcription with separately marked editorial annotations
sources.status: Transcription read; original page not authenticated
sources.readScope: Page 43 text on assumptions, loss estimates and two-circuit tuning; editorial energy-equation commentary kept distinct.
sources.claim: Tesla recorded assumptions, material quantities, revised connections and sharp tuning of interacting oscillations.
sources.limit: This public transcription has weaker provenance than an inspected archival facsimile; it is not an independent replication.
sources.application: Record parameter assumptions and load conditions; show that higher voltage can accompany unchanged total energy.

sources.title: Prospects for Breakthrough Propulsion From Physics — NASA/TM-2004-213082
sources.publisher: Marc G. Millis, NASA Glenn Research Center
sources.readScope: Official PDF: abstract, methods, findings and selected task reports, including 3.1.4 and 3.2.3. Bibliography not independently re-audited.
sources.claim: The 1996–2002 program pursued incremental tests; the report separates non-viable, unresolved and follow-up opportunities.
sources.limit: Instrument interference, an unfinished NASA replication and a separately sponsored null replication are different outcomes. This historical report is not a current breakthrough announcement.
sources.application: Define success as a reliable discriminating result, including a bounded null result.

sources.title: NASA Marshall Space Flight Center Barrel-Shaped Asymmetrical Capacitor
sources.publisher: NASA/TM-2004-213283, Campbell and colleagues
sources.readScope: Official record, PDF contents and section 9, printed p. 45. Full apparatus data and all 62 PDF pages were not audited in this pass.
sources.claim: The authors report thrust in air and no observed performance in hard vacuum; they interpret the observations using ordinary force and momentum mechanisms.
sources.limit: A null is limited by the tested apparatus and sensitivity. No onboard propellant does not mean no momentum exchange with ambient air.
sources.application: Expose environment and momentum boundaries; test a missing-medium control in simulation.

sources.title: Analysis and Assessment of Gateway Process — CIA-RDP96-00788R001700210016-5
sources.publisher: Wayne M. McDonnell, US Army; released record mirrored by Internet Archive
sources.status: Selected OCR passages read; primary host retrieval gap
sources.readScope: Mirror OCR: cover memorandum and sections 6–10. CIA record/PDF links redirected to the reading-room homepage on 2026-10-16; scan symbols not independently verified.
sources.claim: The author proposes connections among auditory beats, bodily resonance and consciousness using analogies and cited models.
sources.limit: The selected passages are an explanatory assessment, not controlled proof of levitation, telepathy, healing or an agency-endorsed physical mechanism.
sources.application: Separate an acoustic signal, a measured neural response and an extraordinary causal interpretation.

sources.title: US10144532B2 — Craft using an inertial mass reduction device
sources.publisher: Salvatore Cezar Pais; original assignee US Department of the Navy
sources.readScope: Publication and original-assignee metadata, proposed cavity/vibration/vacuum mechanism in the description. No new legal-status determination.
sources.claim: The patent proposes that driven electromagnetic and mechanical behavior could produce an inertial-mass effect.
sources.limit: Publication and government assignment establish a proposal, not measured reduction of inertial mass. No independently verified performance dataset was identified in the inspected material.
sources.application: Treat any anomalous force as an additional hypothesis requiring a closed momentum budget and independent calibration.

sources.title: 今日太空实验室｜在轨两年，无容器柜的工作小结
sources.publisher: Chinese Academy of Sciences space-utilization center; source credited to China Manned Space Engineering
sources.readScope: Article and captions covering containerless materials experiments and alloy examples; English descriptions are paraphrases, not certified translations.
sources.claim: The account describes contactless sample processing in the space station’s microgravity environment, including electrostatic levitation experiments.
sources.limit: The rack does not generate orbital microgravity. Institutional reporting is not a raw-data audit or independent replication of every materials claim.
sources.application: Distinguish force-based sample positioning from the environmental gravity condition.

sources.title: CN102384983A — 一种超声悬浮加速度计
sources.publisher: Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics; Chinese patent application
sources.status: Original Chinese description and claims read
sources.readScope: Metadata, mechanism description, force-balance equations (1), (7), (8), and claims 1–3; OCR algebra is not a verified facsimile transcription.
sources.claim: The proposal combines powered near-field acoustic support with capacitive displacement sensing; gravity remains in its balance equation.
sources.limit: A near-field squeeze-film proposal cannot be substituted directly into a far-field standing-wave particle model. Publication alone does not establish calibrated sensor performance.
sources.application: Separate equilibrium height, incremental stiffness, acceleration response and readout calibration.

sources.title: РНФ 17-19-01527 — Magnetic levitation systems based on flexible HTS tapes
sources.publisher: Russian Science Foundation; MEPhI project led by Igor Rudnev
sources.status: Original Russian metadata and abstract read
sources.readScope: Project metadata, author-provided application abstract, proposed magnetic/electrical/thermal model. Listed publications were not independently audited.
sources.claim: The project proposes modeling and testing superconductor–permanent-magnet levitation systems, including thermal and magnetic losses.
sources.limit: A funded project and its author-written aims are not independently verified performance. Contactless support does not remove refrigeration or all dissipation.
sources.application: Retain thermal boundaries and dissipative channels when comparing nominally frictionless devices.

sources.title: RU2539304C2 — Устройство магнитной левитации транспортного средства
sources.publisher: Petersburg State Transport University; Russian patent publication
sources.readScope: Metadata, comparison with onboard drive, proposed powered-track arrangement and operating description; English paraphrase, not certified translation.
sources.claim: The proposal relocates driven rotating magnets to the track and a conductive receiving element to the vehicle.
sources.limit: Avoiding onboard levitation power does not remove the track’s energy input. No independent efficiency dataset was audited.
sources.application: Expand the system boundary to include offboard supplies before calculating efficiency.

sources.title: A comparison of lumped parameter models and Maxwell’s equations for wireless power transfer
sources.publisher: SeMA Journal / Springer Nature
sources.readScope: Full-text abstract, §2, series-series efficiency Eq. 7, parameter estimation and §3 comparison setup inspected.
sources.claim: A two-coil circuit admits a real input-to-load efficiency calculation; fixed lumped parameters can misrepresent distributed eddy-current losses.
sources.limit: Our constant-parameter circuit is not a Maxwell field solve or measured end-to-end charger efficiency.
sources.application: Derives the RLC power-budget check and the explicit boundary for model upgrades.

sources.title: Holographic acoustic elements for manipulation of levitated objects
sources.publisher: Nature Communications
sources.readScope: Results on focusing versus stable traps, holographic lens decomposition, and Methods field-superposition discussion inspected; equation images not re-transcribed.
sources.claim: Phase alignment creates a focus; experimentally useful traps add spatial structure and force-based objectives. The paper reports dense particles being repelled by a simple focus.
sources.limit: Our point sources omit piston directivity, scattering, radiation forces and object dynamics; a bright focus does not certify levitation.
sources.application: Supports conjugate-phase focusing and the focus-versus-trap distinction.

sources.title: Semidefinite programming for manipulating acoustic traps in real time (SMART)
sources.publisher: Scientific Reports; author abstract indexed by PubMed
sources.readScope: Author abstract and publication metadata inspected. Full-text publisher access and institutional PDF retrieval were blocked in this pass.
sources.claim: The authors report semidefinite-programming control of a 256-element array for selected non-spherical Rayleigh objects and Mie spheres.
sources.limit: The browser model does not implement the semidefinite optimizer, force constraints or the experimental apparatus.
sources.application: A documented next step beyond maximizing pressure at one point.

sources.title: Six-degree-of-freedom acoustic manipulation of levitated macroscopic rigid bodies
sources.publisher: Applied Physics Letters / AIP Publishing
sources.readScope: Official publisher search retrieval: article metadata, abstract and selected method/conclusion passages. Direct full-page opening blocked; no complete reproduction audit.
sources.claim: The authors report stationary-array manipulation using a Galerkin boundary-element force/torque model and semidefinite-programming field translation.
sources.limit: This is a specific reported apparatus, not antigravity or evidence that our monopole focus model controls rigid-body motion.
sources.application: Defines missing force, torque, object shape and pose-control layers for a future validated simulator.

sources.title: k-Wave numerical-model documentation
sources.publisher: k-Wave developers
sources.status: Documentation checked on this date; not a new release date
sources.readScope: Overview of governing equations, numerical scheme, attenuation and absorbing boundaries inspected.
sources.claim: The toolbox models time-domain acoustic propagation with heterogeneous media, nonlinear effects and power-law absorption.
sources.limit: k-Wave is an external higher-fidelity option; it is not bundled, executed or validated against our browser model in this release.
sources.application: Upgrade route for boundaries and propagation effects excluded by free-space point-source summation.

sources.title: Lecture 26: Response of 2-DOF Systems by the Use of Transfer Functions
sources.publisher: MIT OpenCourseWare, J. Kim Vandiver
sources.readScope: Official transcript pp. 13–22 inspected: static limit, antiresonance, absorber motion, split modes and damping tradeoffs.
sources.claim: An attached oscillator can cancel primary motion at one drive frequency while introducing two modes and requiring finite absorber stroke.
sources.limit: A frequency-local notch is not broadband isolation. Our added relative-velocity dashpot is specified independently by force balance.
sources.application: Analytic low-frequency and antiresonance checks; compare full response curves instead of one favorable number.

sources.title: The tuned mass-damper-inerter for harmonic vibrations suppression, attached mass reduction, and energy harvesting
sources.publisher: City Research Online / Smart Structures and Systems
sources.readScope: Author abstract and institutional publication record inspected; accepted manuscript not fully audited.
sources.claim: A grounded inerter modifies effective inertia in a driven damper system; the paper also analyzes a generator replacing dissipative damping.
sources.limit: An inerter is not implemented here. Harvested energy would come from external vibration and alter the mechanical load.
sources.application: A bounded future hypothesis: co-optimize vibration reduction and recovered energy with complete source accounting.

sources.title: Theory Manual for the Tuned Mass Damper Module in FAST v8
sources.publisher: William La Cava and Matthew A. Lackner; arXiv author deposit
sources.readScope: Author abstract and version/date note inspected; the full nine-page equations were not audited in this pass.
sources.claim: The manual documents tuned-mass-damper functionality for structural control in the FAST 8 wind-turbine simulator.
sources.limit: A rotating turbine model has coordinate and loading effects beyond our fixed-base two-mass model.
sources.application: Application-scale comparison lead; not used as evidence of current FAST/OpenFAST capabilities.

devices.title: Resonant transfer
devices.subtitle: A source. Two coils. A load.
devices.description: Explore how coupling, detuning, and load resistance change externally powered transfer between two resonators. Account for every watt in this reduced circuit.
devices.formula: Zin = Z₁ + (ωM)²/Z₂ · I₂ = −iωM I₁/Z₂ · Pin = Pload + Ploss
assumptions: Linear series-compensated coils; sinusoidal steady state; RMS voltage and current.
Mutual inductance M = k√(L₁L₂); fixed lumped elements and positive dissipation.
A real external AC source supplies energy. The power balance is at the model source terminals.
limitations: No field solution, coil geometry, eddy currents, saturation, heating, or generator efficiency.
The circuit is inspired by resonant engineering, not a reconstruction of Tesla’s atmospheric-transmission patent.
Efficiency is conditional on this circuit boundary; it is not wall-plug efficiency.
setup: Concept: a driven resonator and separate receiver with a measured resistive load.
Record terminal voltage/current phase on both sides, winding resistance, load power, spacing, and temperature.
Begin with calibrated low-energy instrumentation; the browser supplies no hardware drive signal or construction rating.
Compare coupled and uncoupled states at the same drive, then sweep frequency and report all input and loss channels.

hypotheses.title: Load-aware tuning
hypotheses.useCase: A virtual receiver that retunes when its load changes.
hypotheses.prediction: The frequency with maximum delivered load power need not coincide with the maximum efficiency or isolated coil resonance.
hypotheses.control: Use the same RMS source voltage and coupling; compare a fixed-frequency baseline over the same frequency grid.
hypotheses.falsifier: No improvement beyond measurement uncertainty on an independently sampled sweep, or omitted losses erase the gain.

hypotheses.title: Coupling calibration
hypotheses.useCase: Check a resonator model before planning a coil prototype.
hypotheses.prediction: At fixed geometry, a fitted coupling should predict a second frequency sweep with a different load.
hypotheses.control: Fit only one sweep, freeze the elements, keep spacing and alignment fixed, then evaluate a withheld load. Predicting a new spacing would require a separately calibrated coupling-versus-spacing model.
hypotheses.falsifier: One coupling value cannot predict the withheld complex input impedance at the same geometry within instrument uncertainty.

hypotheses.title: Transient energy ledger
hypotheses.useCase: Test a claimed excess-energy event without confusing storage with generation.
hypotheses.prediction: A complete interval balance includes the change in stored electric and magnetic energy as well as dissipation.
hypotheses.control: Discharge initial storage and measure a source-off baseline. The implemented bench is steady-state; this transient extension is proposed only.
hypotheses.falsifier: An apparent excess disappears when storage, timing, bandwidth, or omitted input paths are included.

connections.note: The circuit model is modern and narrower than the historical patent.
A collector and capacitor do not imply source-free energy.
A proposed optimum is rejected if it breaks the model’s conservation check.

devices.title: Acoustic focus
devices.subtitle: Phase turns an array into a lens.
devices.description: Steer an idealized sound field, change the aperture, and watch phase errors weaken coherence. Inspect the full cross-section rather than only the brightest point.
devices.evidence: Established interference model / proposed measurement rig
devices.formula: p̃(r) ∝ Σ exp[i(φⱼ − krⱼ)]/rⱼ · φⱼ = krⱼ,target
assumptions: Identical isotropic point sources in a homogeneous, lossless medium; single-frequency linear superposition.
The plotted quantity is pressure squared normalized to the ideal target for the same geometry.
A deterministic seeded phase perturbation supports repeatable comparisons.
limitations: No calibrated pascals, sound-pressure level, radiation force, particle scattering, or thermal dose.
A focus is not a stable levitation trap. Stability requires restoring forces and torques in all relevant directions.
No real transducer directivity, enclosure reflections, nonlinear acoustics, or absorption.
setup: Concept: a planar array and scanning pressure probe, with externally powered electronics and an enclosure.
Measure amplitude and phase over a three-dimensional grid; this app displays a selected two-dimensional section.
Compare continuous-phase target settings with phase quantization and calibration error at fixed source strength.
A future trapping experiment would additionally need particle parameters, calibrated force, stability and thermal measurements; it is not implemented here.

hypotheses.title: Spend calibration where it matters
hypotheses.useCase: Choose phase-resolution and calibration tolerances for an array.
hypotheses.prediction: Across repeated phase-error realizations, calibration is expected to preserve target coherence; an individual error can partly cancel a quantization error.
hypotheses.control: Keep source amplitudes fixed; compare ideal continuous phases, quantization only, and error plus quantization over a declared seed set. The interactive display shows one seed.
hypotheses.falsifier: A measured field disagrees with predicted coherence after uncertainty, directivity and reflections are accounted for.

hypotheses.title: Aperture versus ambiguity
hypotheses.useCase: Trade compact hardware against off-target peaks.
hypotheses.prediction: A larger aperture can sharpen the target region, while excessive pitch can introduce additional lobes.
hypotheses.control: Compare full field maps at the same wavelength and target depth; do not renormalize each measured field to its own peak.
hypotheses.falsifier: The apparent focus improvement is only a plotting normalization effect or produces a stronger undesired lobe.

hypotheses.title: From a focus to a trap
hypotheses.useCase: Plan a future force-aware inverse-design study.
hypotheses.prediction: A force-aware optimizer may choose a different field from a pressure-maximizing optimizer.
hypotheses.control: For a specified inert particle, compare all force and torque derivatives and perturbation recovery, not a bright focal image.
hypotheses.falsifier: The candidate lacks a restoring response in any relevant direction. No force-aware solver is implemented in this release.

connections.to: Vary geometry; predict a new field
connections.note: An analogy in method, not a claim that light and sound have identical dynamics.
A mathematical map must state which quantities and boundaries it preserves.
Quantum algorithm results do not supply an acoustic levitation mechanism.

devices.title: Vibration absorber
devices.subtitle: A second oscillator changes the response.
devices.description: Tune an attached spring, mass, and damper to reduce motion of a driven structure. Compare the notch, split peaks, and energy dissipated by each damper.
devices.evidence: Established linear dynamics / proposed adaptive instrument
devices.formula: [K − ω²M + iωC] X = F · Pin = c₁|ωX₁|² + c₂|ω(X₂−X₁)|²
assumptions: Linear springs and viscous dampers; harmonic steady state; RMS force and displacement.
The primary structure has strictly positive damping. Positive masses and stiffnesses define a passive system.
The external force source supplies the average dissipated power.
limitations: No nonlinear stops, actuator delay, friction, changing supports, structural modes, or transient settling.
A deep notch at one frequency can coexist with larger response elsewhere.
A model search is not a measured optimum, patent novelty opinion, or proof of broadband performance.
setup: Concept: an instrumented primary mass with an attached passive spring-mass-damper module.
Measure applied force and both mass motions; compare with the absorber detached at the same drive.
Sweep frequency in both directions and repeat at a second force level to test linearity.
Inspect internal stroke and dissipated power as well as primary motion; simulation parameters are not component ratings.

hypotheses.title: Tune for a band, not one point
hypotheses.useCase: A vibration absorber for a machine whose speed drifts.
hypotheses.prediction: A bounded grid search over tuning and damping can lower the worst sampled response across a declared frequency band.
hypotheses.control: Compare the same unmodified model and use interleaved frequencies excluded from optimization.
hypotheses.falsifier: The gain fails on withheld points, a denser sweep, or measured mounting and parameter uncertainty.

hypotheses.title: Count the hidden stroke
hypotheses.useCase: Screen a tuning that appears attractive at the primary mass.
hypotheses.prediction: A small primary displacement can require appreciable absorber motion and damping power.
hypotheses.control: Report both displacements and the external input power at the same frequency and force.
hypotheses.falsifier: The design exceeds stroke or thermal constraints, even if the primary response is reduced.

hypotheses.title: Use detuning as a diagnostic
hypotheses.useCase: A hypothetical indicator of changing stiffness or mounting.
hypotheses.prediction: A frozen fitted model predicts how a small parameter change moves the response peaks.
hypotheses.control: Measure held-out frequencies and compare stiffness drift with damping or mass changes.
hypotheses.falsifier: Several parameter combinations explain the observations equally well; the inference is then not identifiable.

connections.note: Fitting a response is separate from validating an unseen response.
Related oscillator equations do not make electrical and mechanical devices interchangeable.
A small residual at training points does not guarantee the correct solution elsewhere.
